message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"24aea800aed9042af6da6dc57bb1581615c4747f10c318553b15336a32ef5a6e","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-or-class-c:lineage:50","source_registry_sha256":"ce8335c1d96ff7ed209bf236ba9a56fe92dfebd915bc0e2fa7fb830ee03f0f09","units":[{"unit_id":"sec01-u01","module_id":"sec01-m01","objective_ids":["sec01-u01"],"title":{"text":"Licensing basics and vision","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R16"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Oregon requires a valid driving privilege on highways and on any premises open to the public, so testing is the gateway to legal driving.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01"]},{"text":"Every paid test needs a separate fee and three proofs, so arriving unprepared can cost you the visit.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Nadia wears her glasses for the vision test and reads every line clearly.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Wearing lenses does not fail the test; it adds a requirement to her driving privilege instead.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08"]},"result":{"text":"Nadia passes the vision test, and her privilege will show that she must drive with corrective lenses.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R08"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a failed vision test is an automatic denial that ends the application.","fact_ids":["sec01-R09"]},"correction":{"text":"The vision test is free, and a failing applicant is handed a form to take to a licensed vision specialist.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-R09"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Three tests, one fee each, vision is free.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F05","sec01-R09"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Kim used contact lenses during her vision test and passed. What changes on her privilege?","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]},"answer":{"text":"It shows that she must drive with corrective lenses.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R08"]},"rationale":{"text":"Wearing lenses for the vision test does not fail you; it adds a corrective-lens requirement.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Your path to an Oregon privilege","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Three tests stand between you and driving.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R16"]},{"text":"Preparation starts before the first test.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the first lesson on getting your Oregon driving privilege. Before you can legally drive a motor vehicle on the highways, or on any premises open to the public such as a shopping center lot, you need a valid privilege. This lesson walks through what DMV checks, what you must pay and bring, a special rule for applicants under eighteen, and how the vision test works. Keep in mind that the Oregon Driver Manual is built around one goal, the Class C non-commercial privilege, so everything here points toward that ordinary passenger car license and nothing commercial.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-R16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Three things DMV checks","fact_ids":["sec01-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Your vision.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03"]},{"text":"Your knowledge of driving.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03"]},{"text":"Your driving skill.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"For an original driving privilege, Oregon DMV looks at three separate things. First, can you see well enough to drive. Second, do you know the signs, laws and rules a driver needs. Third, can you actually handle a car on the road. Each of these is its own test, and passing one does not replace another. When a practice question describes a first-time applicant and asks what DMV will test, look for the answer that names all three together. An answer that lists only the knowledge test, or only vision and driving, is leaving something out.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Fees and proofs every time","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Pay the test fee before each test.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]},{"text":"Prove identity, birth date and home address.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]},{"text":"The fee is paid on its own.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Each test comes with homework before you sit down. You must pay the test fee and show proof of three things: who you are, when you were born and where you currently live. That happens before every test, not just the first one. The test fee is also handled by itself, kept apart from any other fee you might owe DMV, so it is never folded into another bill. The good news is convenience. Most DMV offices are able to give the tests, so you are not limited to one special location. Bring the fee and all three proofs every time.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"A rule for younger applicants","fact_ids":["sec01-F36","sec01-R15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Under eighteen and seeking a driver license?","fact_ids":["sec01-F36","sec01-R15"]},{"text":"Hold a permit at least six months first.","fact_ids":["sec01-F36","sec01-R15"]},{"text":"Adults are not bound by this rule.","fact_ids":["sec01-F36","sec01-R15"]}],"narration":{"text":"Younger drivers have one extra requirement in this part of the manual. If you are under eighteen and applying for a driver license, you must have held a permit for at least six months. That six-month permit period is tied to age. It applies to minors seeking a driver license, and it does not apply to adult applicants. Questions like to test this by describing an adult first-time applicant and asking whether the permit clock applies. It does not. Pay attention to the applicant's age in any scenario before deciding whether the six months matter.","fact_ids":["sec01-F36","sec01-R15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Glasses are not a failure","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Lenses add a requirement.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R08"]},{"text":"They do not fail you.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap many learners fall into. Wearing glasses or contact lenses during the vision test does not count against you. It simply means your driving privilege will show a corrective-lens requirement, so from then on you must drive with those lenses. The opposite mistake also shows up, which is believing that wearing lenses leaves no mark at all. It does leave a mark, just not a failing one. If a question asks what happens to someone who tested with contacts and passed, the answer is a corrective-lens requirement, not a failure and not a clean record.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your vision rules","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R08","sec01-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"A passing applicant wore contacts.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R08","sec01-F07"]},{"text":"What appears on the privilege?","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R08","sec01-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: Kim used contact lenses during her vision test and read the chart well enough to pass. What changes on her driving privilege? Think about the lens rule before you answer. The answer is that her privilege will show she must drive with corrective lenses. Wearing lenses for the vision test does not fail you, and it does not leave the privilege unmarked either. It adds a requirement. Now compare that with an applicant who truly fails the vision test. That person is not simply denied. They receive a form to take to a licensed vision specialist.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R08","sec01-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"What to carry forward","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R16","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F36","sec01-F07","sec01-R09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Privilege needed on public premises.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R16","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F36","sec01-F07","sec01-R09"]},{"text":"Three tests, fee and proofs each time.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R16","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F36","sec01-F07","sec01-R09"]},{"text":"Vision test free, with a specialist form.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R16","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F36","sec01-F07","sec01-R09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us gather the lesson. You need a valid privilege to drive on highways and on premises open to the public, and this manual covers only the Class C non-commercial privilege, so commercial rules live elsewhere. DMV tests vision, knowledge and driving skill. Before each test you pay a separately handled fee and prove identity, birth date and address. Applicants under eighteen seeking a driver license must hold a permit for six months first. The vision test stands apart from the others because it is free, and failing it brings a referral form for a licensed vision specialist.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-R16","sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F36","sec01-F07","sec01-R09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec01-u02","module_id":"sec01-m02","objective_ids":["sec01-u02"],"title":{"text":"The taker use during an office knowledge test if staff give permission?","fact_ids":["sec01-F13"]},"answer":{"text":"A paper foreign-language translation dictionary.","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R05"]},"rationale":{"text":"A DMV manual, notes and electronic devices are banned outright, so the paper dictionary is the only aid that permission can bring.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on the Class C knowledge test. This test checks what you know about road signs, traffic laws and the other things every driver needs, and the manual is designed to hold all of that material. In this lesson you will learn how many questions there are and the passing standard, the ways you can take the test, who is allowed in the office testing area, which aids are permitted and which are banned, and what counts as cheating. These rules are simple, but each one is a favorite target for tricky practice questions.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Questions and the passing standard","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Thirty five multiple-choice questions.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F08"]},{"text":"Twenty eight correct answers pass the test.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"The Class C knowledge test is made of thirty five multiple-choice questions. The passing standard is twenty eight correct answers. Those two numbers belong together, so learn them as a pair: thirty five asked and twenty eight right. Practice questions often swap in near-miss numbers, such as a test of forty questions or a passing mark of twenty five, so anchor on the exact pair. Remember too what the questions are about. They draw on road signs, traffic laws and the other knowledge a driver must have, and the manual is written to contain everything the test covers.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Where and how you test","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F12","sec01-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Online through DMV two U, at any hour.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F12","sec01-F17"]},{"text":"At an office as a standby walk-in.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F12","sec01-F17"]},{"text":"At an office by appointment.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F12","sec01-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"You have choices about where to take the knowledge test. You can take it online through DMV two U at any hour of the day or night, or you can go to a DMV office, either as a walk-in waiting on standby or with an appointment. Office tests run on a touch-screen monitor and come in several languages, with or without audio, and you may bring your own earbuds or headphones to listen. If you need a special accommodation to take the test, the step is to contact your local DMV office ahead of time so the office can plan for it.","fact_ids":["sec01-F10","sec01-F12","sec01-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Allowed aids versus banned aids","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R05","sec01-F11","sec01-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Paper translation dictionary: only with permission.","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R05","sec01-F11","sec01-R04"]},{"text":"DMV manual, notes, devices: never.","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R05","sec01-F11","sec01-R04"]},{"text":"Translators: test area yes, car no.","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R05","sec01-F11","sec01-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"This is where many learners get caught. During the knowledge test you may not use a DMV manual, notes or any electronic device. There is a single narrow exception, a paper foreign-language translation dictionary, and even that needs permission. A phone translation app does not qualify, because it is an electronic device. A second trap involves translators. In the office testing area, the only people allowed are those being tested and authorized translators. That permission stays in the office. A translator may never ride in the car during the drive test, where only you and the examiner belong.","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R05","sec01-F11","sec01-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the aid rules","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R05","sec01-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Staff can approve one aid.","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R05","sec01-F14"]},{"text":"Which one is it?","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R05","sec01-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: which item could a test taker use during an office knowledge test if staff give permission? Run through the banned list first. A DMV manual is not allowed. Notes are not allowed. Electronic devices, including phones, are not allowed. What remains is a paper foreign-language translation dictionary, and that is the answer, as long as permission is given. Now go one step further. Talking, writing or taking notes, using a cell phone or any electronic device, or having someone else take the test for you are all treated as cheating, not as small slips.","fact_ids":["sec01-F13","sec01-R05","sec01-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Knowledge test essentials","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F14","sec01-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Thirty five questions, twenty eight correct pass.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F14","sec01-F17"]},{"text":"Online any hour, or at an office.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F14","sec01-F17"]},{"text":"No manual, notes or devices.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F14","sec01-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us wrap up the knowledge test essentials. The test covers road signs, traffic laws and other driver knowledge. It has thirty five multiple-choice questions, and the passing standard is twenty eight correct. You can take it online through DMV two U at any hour, or at an office on standby or by appointment, where it runs on a touch screen in several languages with optional audio. Only test takers and authorized translators may be in the testing area. A DMV manual, notes and devices are banned, a paper translation dictionary needs permission, and a stand-in tester counts as cheating.","fact_ids":["sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-F11","sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F14","sec01-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec01-u03","module_id":"sec01-m03","objective_ids":["sec01-u03"],"title":{"text":"Cheating, retests and online testing","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-R01"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The penalty for cheating is far heavier than an ordinary failure, so knowing the difference protects your timeline.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01"]},{"text":"Online testing has its own device, identity, proctor and attempt rules that differ from office testing.","fact_ids":["sec01-F18","sec01-F20","sec01-F21"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ella, who is under eighteen, plans to take the knowledge test online at home with her aunt as proctor.","fact_ids":["sec01-F20"]},"reasoning":{"text":"The proctor must be over twenty one, and one proctor may supervise no more than two tests in any twenty four hour period.","fact_ids":["sec01-F20","sec01-R07"]},"result":{"text":"Ella can test with her aunt only if her aunt is over twenty one and has not already proctored two tests that day.","fact_ids":["sec01-F20"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking any licensed adult can proctor an online test for a minor.","fact_ids":["sec01-R07"]},"correction":{"text":"The proctor must be over twenty one, not just any licensed adult, and the rule applies to online test takers under eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec01-R07","sec01-F20"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Cheat and wait ninety days.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-R01"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Two office test takers fail on the same morning, one of them for cheating. Which one might retest that day?","fact_ids":["sec01-R01"]},"answer":{"text":"Only the one with an ordinary failure, if the office has testing capacity.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F16"]},"rationale":{"text":"An ordinary office failure may allow a same-day retest by capacity, while cheating bars retesting for ninety days.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F15"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"When a test goes wrong","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-F21"]},"lines":[{"text":"Cheating carries a heavy penalty.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-F21"]},{"text":"Ordinary failures can be quicker to fix.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-F21"]},{"text":"Online testing has its own limits.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-F21"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on cheating, retests and online testing. Not every knowledge test ends with a pass, and what happens next depends on why it ended the way it did. An ordinary failure and a cheating failure lead to very different waits. The online version of the test also comes with its own rules: the kind of computer you need, how your identity is confirmed, who must supervise younger test takers, and how many attempts you get before an office visit is required. Each of these has a number attached, so keep them in separate boxes in your mind.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-F21"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Cheating versus an ordinary failure","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Caught cheating: fail and wait ninety days.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-R01"]},{"text":"Ordinary office failure: maybe retest same day.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-R01"]},{"text":"Same-day depends on office capacity.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Anyone caught cheating fails the knowledge test and must wait ninety days before testing again. That is a hard stop. An ordinary failure at an office is gentler. You may be able to retest on the same day, but only if that office has enough testing capacity to fit you in, so it is a possibility rather than a promise. When a scenario describes a failure, first ask why the person failed. If cheating was involved, the ninety day wait applies no matter how empty the office is. If it was an ordinary failure, the same-day retest depends on capacity.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The right device online","fact_ids":["sec01-F18","sec01-R06","sec01-F19"]},"lines":[{"text":"Desktop or laptop with keyboard, mouse, webcam.","fact_ids":["sec01-F18","sec01-R06","sec01-F19"]},{"text":"No phones, tablets or touchscreens.","fact_ids":["sec01-F18","sec01-R06","sec01-F19"]},{"text":"Office tests use a touch-screen monitor.","fact_ids":["sec01-F18","sec01-R06","sec01-F19"]}],"narration":{"text":"The online knowledge test needs a desktop or laptop computer that has a keyboard, a mouse and a webcam. Phones, tablets and other touchscreen devices cannot be used, even if they have good cameras. That is the reverse of the office, where the test runs on a DMV touch-screen monitor. So touchscreens are fine at the office and off limits at home. The webcam has a job too. It takes a clear photo of you when the online test begins and random photos while you work, all to confirm that the person taking the test is really you and nobody else.","fact_ids":["sec01-F18","sec01-R06","sec01-F19"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Proctors for younger test takers","fact_ids":["sec01-F20","sec01-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Online and under eighteen: proctor required.","fact_ids":["sec01-F20","sec01-R07"]},{"text":"Proctor must be over twenty one.","fact_ids":["sec01-F20","sec01-R07"]},{"text":"No more than two tests per day.","fact_ids":["sec01-F20","sec01-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"If you are under eighteen and taking the knowledge test online, a proctor must supervise you. The proctor must be over twenty one. That is a specific age line, not simply any licensed adult. The two ages in this rule describe different people. Under eighteen describes the test taker who needs supervision, and over twenty one describes the person doing the supervising. There is also a cap on proctors themselves. One proctor may supervise no more than two tests in any twenty four hour period, so a busy parent with several teens cannot proctor all of them in one day.","fact_ids":["sec01-F20","sec01-R07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Online attempts are counted","fact_ids":["sec01-F21","sec01-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two tries within a day.","fact_ids":["sec01-F21","sec01-R02"]},{"text":"Four tries in total.","fact_ids":["sec01-F21","sec01-R02"]},{"text":"After the fourth, go to an office.","fact_ids":["sec01-F21","sec01-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap with online retesting. Office retests depend on capacity, but online retests are counted. Online, you may test twice within a twenty four hour period and four times in total. After the fourth online attempt, you must take the test at a DMV office. Learners often blend this with the office rule and assume online attempts are unlimited as long as you wait a day. They are not. Watch for distractors that offer four tries in a day, or a ninety day wait after the fourth attempt. The ninety days belong only to cheating, and the next step after four is an office.","fact_ids":["sec01-F21","sec01-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the retest rules","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F15","sec01-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two failures, one for cheating.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F15","sec01-F16"]},{"text":"Who might retest today?","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F15","sec01-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: two office test takers fail on the same morning, and one of them failed because of cheating. Which one might be able to retest that day? The answer is only the person with an ordinary failure, and only if the office has testing capacity left. The cheater has failed and must wait ninety days before testing again, no matter how quiet the office is. Keep this contrast sharp, because the reason for the failure, not the clock or the office schedule, is what sets the wait.
